item.title: Nepal’s glacial collapse foreshadowed a future of climate disaster | Michael Mann
item.description: The deluge capped a summer of extreme climate events, from deadly heatwaves to wildfires. We must take action now For millennia, the high peaks of the Himalayas were held together by an invisible, frozen cement – permafrost and glacial ice that bound ancient rock into seemingly unshakable fortresses. But as the planet continues to warm, this alpine glue is liquefying. The glacial collapse and deluge in Nepal and Tibet was not a freak weather event ; it was the structural failure of a mountain itself, nature’s latest commentary on the deadly consequences of human-caused planetary warming. And… Fuente: The Guardian - Environment.

item.title: 'Glaciers in Himalayas retreating': Nepal floods triggered by 'glacier collapse & massive landslide'
item.description: Annette Young is pleased to welcome Joseph Shea, Glaciologist and Associate Professor at the University of Northern BC. Shea argues that the catastrophe should be understood as a compound event in which a glacier failure and a massive landslide occurred together. His analysis places the disaster within the broader, well-established transformation of the Himalayas under climate change. As warming changes high-mountain environments, scientists may increasingly need to identify subtle precursors to rare but potentially devastating cascading hazards. Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.title: Cities sweltering and the smell of the middle ages: has the climate crisis killed Instagram’s Euro summer? | Brigid Delaney
item.description: Who dreams of having a Euro summer now when staying in an ancient, uncooled building in the Old Town is like trying to sleep in a wood-fired pizza oven? This week the Euro summer comes to an end – and so does a certain type of posting on Instagram. Waiting at the bus stop in the grey winter dawn, a slanting rain soaking your trouser leg, you can warm yourself by scrolling your feed and seeing pictures of Australians enjoying a Euro summer. There it is again – azure Greek coves, plates of barbecued sardines, the yachts rented by the hour, and selfies on the balcony of some Paris Airbnb… Fuente: The Guardian - Environment.

item.description: In Alaska, the Himalayas, the Andes, Greenland, and perhaps also the Alps, deadly chain reactions are just waiting to be triggered You may not have felt it, but the earth beneath our feet is getting twitchier, and global heating is to blame. As temperatures surge and climate breakdown accelerates, interactions between climate and geology are becoming ever more apparent – as marked by last week’s horrific events in Nepal and Tibet . item.title: Brazil’s humpback whales make stunning comeback; population surges from just 2,000 to nearly 35,000
item.description: Brazil’s humpback whale population has recovered from about 2,000 to nearly 35,000 after commercial whaling pushed the species close to extinction. Protection measures and a global whaling ban helped the whales return to Brazil’s waters. Scientists are now studying their migration, family links and behaviour, while tracking threats from fishing nets, ships and warming seas. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: New policy brief outlines how EU policies can better support sponge restoration
item.description: Europe's water and climate resilience is under increasing pressure, with degraded soils, drained catchments and the loss of wetlands intensifying droughts and contributing to more destructive floods. item.description: El bloque comunitario dijo “no” a las importaciones de carne de vacuno y aves de corral procedentes de Brasil por incumplimientos de sus normas sanitarias sobre el uso de antibióticos. item.description: Detenido en Bolivia y acusado de ser el autor intelectual de un intento de feminicidio contra su expareja, Fernando Cerimedo volvió al centro de la escena. El consultor argentino tejió vínculos con figuras de la derecha latinoamericana, como Javier Milei, Jair Bolsonaro, Rodrigo Paz y el entorno de José Antonio Kast. ¿Cómo construyó poder este polémico asesor que logró acercarse a algunos de los principales líderes de la derecha regional? item.title: IncaDivide 2026: el Everest del ultraciclismo en el Valle Sagrado de los Incas en Perú
item.description: El 29 de agosto terminó el IncaDivide de Urubamba, en Perú. Se trata de una de las carreras de ciclismo de ultradistancia más exigentes, en donde los participantes recorrieron 1.200 km por rutas en grava en nueve días sin asistencia externa y en autosuficiencia total a través de los Andes peruanos. Cada corredor debía gestionar sus horas de sueño, su comida, cuántos kilómetros recorría al día y qué equipaje llevar. El francés Pierre Rolland fue el ganador y la leyenda peruana Rodney Soncco quedó segundo. Fuente: France 24 - Español.
item.dc:creator: Natalia Ruiz Giraldo

item.title: EU suspends Brazilian meat imports over antibiotic compliance concerns
item.description: The European Union will suspend imports of Brazilian meat and other animal products from Thursday, citing concerns over Brazil’s compliance with EU rules on antibiotic use in livestock. The move affects poultry, beef, eggs and honey, with Brussels offering no timeline for when trade can resume. Fuente: France 24 - English.
